text:
anya: Heads-up — nightly eval (nightly-2026-03-19) shows a regression on our zh->ko anchored translation subset. Anchor match F1 dropped ~0.12 absolute vs baseline. Looks concentrated on honorific/title tokens and simp->trad pathways.

devin: Which model/variant is failing? quantized or float?

anya: Failing primarily on redwood-model-3b-v2-8bit (our q4-ish pipeline). Baseline redwood-model-3b-v2-f16 is fine.

mike.zhang: Can you paste 2-3 concrete examples? especially where titles/honorifics change.

anya: Example 1:
```
SRC (zh): 我昨天把报告发给张总，他说会在下周二前回复。
REF (ko): 어제 보고서를 장 부장님께 보냈고, 그는 다음 주 화요일까지 회신하겠다고 했습니다.
OUT (v2-f16): 어제 보고서를 장 부장님께 보냈고, 그는 다음 주 화요일까지 답장을 하겠다고 했습니다.
OUT (v2-8bit): 어제 리포트를 장 사장님에게 보냈는데, 그는 다음 주 화요일 전에 답할 거라고 했어요.
```
Notes: v2-8bit switches honorific (张总 -> 사장님) and tone (adds casual ending).

anya: Example 2:
```
SRC (zh): 请转告主管李老师，这件事需要尽快处理。
REF (ko): 담당자 이 선생님께 전해 주세요. 이 사안은 신속하게 처리해야 합니다.
OUT (v2-f16): 담당자 이 선생님에게 전달해 주세요. 이 사안은 신속히 처리해야 합니다.
OUT (v2-8bit): 담당자 리 선생님께 전해주세요. 이건 빨리 처리해야 해요.
```
Notes: again v2-8bit adopts more colloquial phrasing and slightly different name tokenization (李 -> 리 vs translit mapping).

sophia: That's concerning. Our BLEU stayed flat but anchor F1 / named-entity match dropped. We need targeted metrics for titles/honorifics.

devin: Quick hypothesis: quantization changed embedding centroids for certain multi-character name/title token pairs (e.g., '张'+'总'), and the tokenizer merge behavior between simp/trad causes different token boundaries. Combined they push different high-prob tokens.

anya: I ran tokenizer stats for the anchor subset:
```
baseline f16: avg token length src=1.24, anchor_hit=0.81
v2-8bit: avg token length src=1.35, anchor_hit=0.62
```
Different token length distribution suggests merges/splits.

mike.zhang: Can we re-run the nightly eval with the exact baseline tokenization pipeline but with quantized weights to isolate where the regression comes from? Also check whether we applied any simp->trad normalization in the new pipeline.

eval-bot: queued re-eval job 1782489150 for model=redwood-model-3b-v2-8bit token_pipeline=baseline-tokenizer (status: queued)

devin: I'll take bisect. Plan:
1) Run quantized weights + baseline tokenizer
2) Run f16 weights + new tokenizer pipeline
3) Check caching/prefix behavior on canaries
ETA ~2-3 hours for quick-run subset.

anya: Please hold any canary release if this persists. Blocking flag on canary until we confirm anchor metrics recover. @eng-oncall FYI.

eng-oncall-bot: canary 1782489180 placed on hold (reason: nightly anchor regression).

devin: Early bisect result: step (1) quantized weights w/ baseline tokenizer reproduces ~70% of the drop. Weight quantization seems to shift logits on tokens that represent title compounds.

sophia: If quantization is the culprit, try tuning per-channel scales for embedding/mapping layers or rerun with 6-bit mixed precision for embeddings. Also add a targeted eval for named-entity/honorific preservation to nightly.

mike.zhang: I'll add the targeted eval (small set ~1.2k anchors) and a prompt-level rule that flags honorific mismatches.

anya: Thanks. Keep notes here as you run the experiments so we can decide rollback vs model fix. Short replies preferred so we can triage fast.

devin: Will post logs + diff of embedding nearest neighbours after run. If anyone has quick ideas for temporary mitigations: disable the simp->trad conversion and force a consistent normalization step for the pipeline used by canaries.

anya: Agreed. Also tag anyone from infra if we need a hotfix to push different tokenizers to canaries.

mike.zhang: ack — pinging eng-infra after we confirm the re-eval.

anya: End of thread for now — will update with eval-bot job result.
